```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 7)
```

Control measures change the model's inputs. Vaccination (idealised here as
giving full immunity) moves people straight into the R compartment before the
outbreak, and measures like distancing reduce $\beta$.

```{r}
library(deSolve)

sir <- function(time, state, parms) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parms)), {
    dS <- -beta * S * I / N
    dI <-  beta * S * I / N - gamma * I
    dR <-  gamma * I
    list(c(dS, dI, dR))
  })
}

# Run an epidemic where a fraction `vacc` of the population starts immune
run_sir <- function(beta = 0.5, gamma = 0.2, N = 1000, vacc = 0, days = 200) {
  start <- c(S = N - vacc * N - 1, I = 1, R = vacc * N)
  as.data.frame(ode(start, seq(0, days, by = 1), sir,
                    c(beta = beta, gamma = gamma, N = N)))
}
```

# Compare vaccination coverage

With $R_0 = 2.5$ the herd immunity threshold is $1 - 1/2.5 = 0.6$.

```{r}
coverage <- c(0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7)
cols <- c("black", "blue", "darkgreen", "red")

plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 200), ylim = c(0, 350),
     xlab = "Day", ylab = "Infectious people")
for (i in seq_along(coverage)) {
  out <- run_sir(vacc = coverage[i])
  lines(out$time, out$I, col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
}
legend("topright", paste0(coverage * 100, "% vaccinated"), col = cols, lwd = 2)
```

At 70% coverage (above the 60% threshold) the single introduced case cannot
start an epidemic.

# How many people are infected at each coverage level?

```{r}
infected_by_coverage <- function(p) {
  out <- run_sir(vacc = p)
  tail(out$R, 1) - p * 1000          # recovered minus those vaccinated
}

p_grid <- seq(0, 0.9, by = 0.05)
total_infected <- sapply(p_grid, infected_by_coverage)

plot(p_grid, total_infected, type = "b", pch = 16,
     xlab = "Vaccination coverage", ylab = "People infected (of 1000)")
abline(v = 0.6, lty = 2)
```

# Reducing transmission instead

A 40% cut in contacts lowers $\beta$ from 0.5 to 0.3, so $R_0$ falls from 2.5
to 1.5:

```{r}
base  <- run_sir(beta = 0.5)
cut40 <- run_sir(beta = 0.3)
c(peak_baseline = round(max(base$I)), peak_with_distancing = round(max(cut40$I)))
```

Distancing flattens and delays the peak even when it does not stop the
epidemic.
